newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Aokam profit fall due to high overheads.
newsitem.headline: Aokam profit fall due to high overheads.

text.p: Malaysian logging firm Aokam Perdana Bhd said the sharp profit fall for its 1996 financial year was due to high overhead costs at its plant, which were caused by an insufficent supply of logs.

Unfavourable weather conditions in the logging areas also hampered extraction and transportation of logs from the company's concession areas, the company said in a release accompanying its results which were released on Tuesday.
The company reported a loss of 144.73 million ringgit for the year ended June 30, 1996, against a 47.04 million profit in the previous year.
These "resulted in insufficient log supply to the plant and deterioration in the quality of logs delivered", Aokam said.
"The production volume achieved (at the plant) which represented about 30 percent to 40 percent of the targeted level had resulted in a very high fixed production overheads.
"In addition, the inability to achieve the targeted volume also resulted in an abnormally high labour content in our cost of production," it said.
Aokam said although response to its marketing efforts has been very encouraing, it has to forego "a lot of sales opportunities" as production volume was below expectation.

It said the company will downsize the original planned production target and streamline both operating and administrative manpower requirement to achieve production efficiency and a lower production cost.
"Alternative sources of log supply are identified to ensure the plant is running at its revised capacity," Aokam said.
